assignments.question: Identify the warehouse-specific conditions to assess for forklift–pedestrian separation (traffic routes, crossing points, visibility, congestion, work tasks, and existing controls); flag which site facts are needed before judging adequacy.

Check the applicable OSHA powered-industrial-truck provisions relevant to pedestrian interaction and travel, especially 29 CFR 1910.178(c)(2)(D) and 1910.178(n)(4); provide exact clauses and any applicability/effective-date limits, without claiming compliance from the limited cache excerpt.

assignments.question: Identify the warehouse and work context to check when assessing forklift–pedestrian separation: pedestrian routes and crossing points, truck routes and operating areas, visibility/blind spots, traffic intensity and layout, and whether workers or visitors enter vehicle areas. Point out which site-specific facts are not supplied.

Locate and summarize the relevant OSHA references for forklift–pedestrian interaction, especially 29 CFR 1910.178 provisions on pedestrian traffic, operator precautions and training/workplace evaluation; check related aisle/material-handling standards where relevant. Provide exact citations and distinguish binding standards from OSHA guidance; flag any applicability or source-text limitations.

Identify the operational/site context needed to assess forklift–pedestrian separation in the US warehouse: warehouse layout and routes, pedestrian and truck interactions, controls already in use, and whether the work falls under federal OSHA or a state plan. Do not make a legal applicability conclusion; flag unknowns.

Find relevant primary OSHA references for forklift–pedestrian separation, especially powered industrial truck rules and any related walking-working surface or traffic-control provisions. Provide exact source-linked references and concise summaries; distinguish binding text from OSHA guidance and note that applicability and full context remain to be verified.
